lesson.title: Cubital fossa and forearm compartments
lesson.summary: Most anterior forearm muscles receive median supply, but flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial part of flexor digitorum profundus are ulnar exceptions.

steps.title: Cubital Fossa and Forearm Compartments
steps.body: The cubital fossa is the anterior elbow triangle. Its deep contents are biceps tendon, brachial artery, median nerve, and radial nerve laterally; the median cubital vein is superficial.

steps.title: Relationships and functional organization
steps.body: Borders: superior interepicondylar line, medial pronator teres, lateral brachioradialis. Floor: brachialis and supinator. Roof: cubital fascia and bicipital aponeurosis. Anterior forearm is mainly flexor-pronator and mostly median nerve. FCU and medial half of FDP are ulnar nerve. Posterior forearm is extensor-supinator and radial/deep radial/posterior interosseous nerve.

steps.title: Why is pronation-supination not simply rotation of the hand at the wrist?
steps.body: The radius rotates relative to ulna at proximal and distal radioulnar joints, carrying the hand with it. In pronation the radius crosses the ulna; in supination they are approximately parallel. The wrist articulations then position the hand on this rotating framework. Supinator and biceps contribute to supination, while pronator teres and quadratus contribute to pronation. A drawing that puts all rotation at the radiocarpal joint would miss the long-bone mechanics and the two radioulnar articulations.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: Most anterior forearm muscles receive median supply, but flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial part of flexor digitorum profundus are ulnar exceptions. The posterior compartment uses radial-derived branches. In the cubital fossa, biceps tendon, brachial artery and median nerve lie in a lateral-to-medial sequence, with the radial nerve farther laterally. The bicipital aponeurosis separates deeper neurovascular structures from superficial veins. Surface and deep structures must be placed in separate layers.
